raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With attention DP and TP MoE on CUDA, the MoE input of a decode step is a MAX_LEN gather: every DP rank contributes a slot of the same length, and the rows past its real requests are padding. The decode CUDA graph always uses this layout, and an idle rank still replays one fabricated row. The router sends the padding rows to experts like real tokens, so every MoE layer loads those experts' weights.

Since #46225 this costs more on hybrid models. Before it, the unpacked KDA/GDN decode left the padding rows' output unwritten. On GLM-5.3-Flash, six or seven of the seven padding rows of a one-request step then selected exactly experts 0-7 in every MoE layer, which is what the router does with NaN scores (it ranks NaN as -1e30 and breaks ties toward the lowest id). #46225 zeroes that output, which is the right fix for correctness, and the padding rows now route like real tokens. With one request on 8×H20 (attention DP8), the expert-distribution recorder counts about 41 distinct experts per MoE layer per decode step instead of about 22, and median ITL went from 11.84 ms (main before #46225) to 12.73 ms (main).

On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4 zeroes the padding rows before the gather (#43077). Zeroed rows still route, to the experts with the largest correction bias. This PR keeps them out of routing.

`SGLANG_OPT_MASK_DP_PAD_MOE` (#31888, off by default) drops the same rows from the dispatch, but only with EP: it runs in the standard dispatcher after the local expert mapping, which exists only when `moe_ep_size > 1`. With TP MoE the rows still route.

## Modifications

- `ForwardBatch.dp_real_rows_gpu` (int64, one count per DP rank) holds how many rows of each rank's slot are real, when the MoE input is a MAX_LEN decode gather. Eager decode writes it in `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`, in the same `write_host_ints` launch as `global_num_tokens_gpu`. The decode CUDA graph keeps a static copy and refreshes it on every replay with a device copy of the batch's `global_num_tokens_gpu`, which still holds the per-rank counts because the graph path skips `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`. `ForwardContext.moe_dp_real_rows` exposes it the way `moe_num_token_non_padded` is exposed.
- `select_experts` (CUDA, standard top-k output) sets the padding rows' ids to -1:
  - The Triton router `moe_fused_gate` does it inside its existing launch (`HAS_DP_ROWS`, next to `HAS_PADDING`). `select_experts` hands it the counts on the biased sigmoid / sqrtsoftplus path and on the two Triton-router branches of `biased_grouped_topk_gpu`; GLM-5.3-Flash takes the grouped one.
  - The router's two fast paths, every other router, and an EPLB remap (which would read -1 as its last entry) get one `_fill_dp_pad_rows` launch afterwards. A separate launch per MoE layer is not free: an earlier revision that always masked after the router cost 0.3-0.6% ITL at 8-128 concurrent requests on GLM-5.3-Flash DP8.
- The Triton fused MoE already skips -1 ids (the EP convention), so padding rows load no expert weights and return zeros. Real rows are unchanged bit for bit with BF16 activations and with per-token or per-group activation scales (GLM-5.3-Flash's block FP8). With per-tensor dynamic FP8 (no static `a2_scale`), the down GEMM's activation scale no longer covers the padding rows, so real rows can move by FP8 rounding.
- Scope (`_dp_tp_moe_skips_pad_rows`): CUDA; attention DP > 1 with attention TP = 1, so each rank owns one contiguous slot; no attention CP; TP MoE (EP 1, no A2A, FP4 all-gather or DWDP); no world DP gather; no two-batch overlap; non-speculative decode. `SGLANG_DP_MASK_PAD_ROWS=false` turns it off; ROCm uses the same switch for its zeroing.
- MoE runners: tested with the Triton fused MoE. The CUTLASS MoE path also treats ids outside [0, num_experts) as unused (`cutlass_prepare_moe_input`), and `flashinfer_trtllm` with in-kernel routing never sees them. Not checked: the FlashInfer CUTLASS runner and `flashinfer_trtllm` with precomputed routing.
- Not covered yet: speculative decode (verify batches carry several rows per request) and prefill steps with an idle rank (its fabricated extend rows). The same masking applies to both, with counts in rows instead of requests.
- Tests, `test/registered/moe/test_topk_padded_region.py::TestDpPadRows`:
  - `_fill_dp_pad_rows` against an eager reference over three layouts, each with an idle rank;
  - the same kernel captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with changing counts;
  - `moe_fused_gate` with `dp_real_rows`, with and without a fused shared expert;
  - `select_experts` + `fused_moe` under a forward context with DP counts, for a softmax router, a biased sigmoid router and a grouped biased sigmoid router, both with a fused shared expert: padding rows get -1 and zero output, and real rows match the unmasked run bit for bit. Dropping the mask after the router, or the counts from a Triton-router call, fails this test.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_topk_padded_region.py` on H20: 13 passed, 3 HIP-only skipped, 56 subtests.
- GSM8K, attention DP8 (8-shot completion, all 1,319 questions, greedy, 512 tokens): main 0.931 / 0.933; this PR 0.923, and 0.936 / 0.928 for the earlier revision, which sends the same rows to -1 after the router instead of inside it.
- Greedy output ids on a fixed 1024-token prompt are identical to main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GLM-5.3-Flash on 8×H20, main c0c7af402b, attention DP8, no MTP, TileLang DSA, BF16 KV cache, 1024-token random prompts, 256-512 output tokens; median ITL, two servers per version.

| Concurrency | main | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.73 / 12.73 ms | 11.34 / 11.34 ms | -10.9% |
| 8 | 12.80 / 12.80 ms | 12.82 / 12.81 ms | +0.1% |
| 16 | 14.53 / 14.52 ms | 14.52 / 14.54 ms | 0.0% |
| 64 | 19.61 / 19.69 ms | 19.71 / 19.69 ms | +0.3% |
| 128 | 23.33 / 23.37 ms | 23.32 / 23.41 ms | +0.1% |

From 8 concurrent requests up every rank usually has the same number of requests, so there are few padding rows to skip.

Without attention DP nothing changes: the counts are never built and `select_experts` skips the mask.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -110,3 +110,61 @@ def _fill_padded_rows(
         BLOCK_COLS=triton.next_power_of_2(n_cols),
         STRIDED=strided,
     )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _fill_dp_pad_rows_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    dp_real_rows_ptr,
+    rows_per_rank,
+    n_cols,
+    fill_value,
+    stride_row,
+    BLOCK_COLS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # One program per row. DP rank r owns rows [r * rows_per_rank,
+    # (r + 1) * rows_per_rank); the first dp_real_rows[r] of them are real.
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    rank = row // rows_per_rank
+    if row - rank * rows_per_rank >= tl.load(dp_real_rows_ptr + rank):
+        cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_COLS)
+        ptrs = out_ptr + row.to(tl.int64) * stride_row + cols
+        fill = tl.full((BLOCK_COLS,), fill_value, dtype=out_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+        tl.store(ptrs, fill, mask=cols < n_cols)
+
+
+def _fill_dp_pad_rows(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    dp_real_rows: torch.Tensor,
+    fill_value,
+) -> None:
+    """Set ``x[row, :] = fill_value`` for the padding rows of a MAX_LEN DP gather.
+
+    ``x`` holds one equal slot per DP rank, in rank order, and slot ``r`` starts
+    with ``dp_real_rows[r]`` real rows. The counts are read from device memory,
+    so this is safe to capture inside a CUDA graph.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(dp_real_rows, torch.Tensor):
+        raise TypeError("dp_real_rows must be a torch.Tensor")
+    if dp_real_rows.dim() != 1 or dp_real_rows.dtype.is_floating_point:
+        raise TypeError(
+            "dp_real_rows must be a 1-D integer tensor, got "
+            f"{dp_real_rows.dtype} {tuple(dp_real_rows.shape)}"
+        )
+    if dp_real_rows.device != x.device:
+        raise ValueError("dp_real_rows and x must be on the same device")
+    n_rows, n_cols = x.shape
+    num_ranks = dp_real_rows.numel()
+    if num_ranks == 0 or n_rows % num_ranks != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{n_rows} rows do not split into {num_ranks} equal DP slots")
+    if n_rows == 0:
+        return
+    _fill_dp_pad_rows_kernel[(n_rows,)](
+        x,
+        dp_real_rows,
+        n_rows // num_ranks,
+        n_cols,
+        fill_value,
+        x.stride(0),
+        BLOCK_COLS=triton.next_power_of_2(n_cols),
+    )

+            (num_ranks,), rows_per_rank, device=self.DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        work = ids.clone()
+        side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            _fill_dp_pad_rows(work.clone(), counts, -1)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            _fill_dp_pad_rows(work, counts, -1)
+
+        for step in ([4] * 8, [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 2, 4, 1, 3, 0, 4, 1]):
+            work.copy_(ids)
+            counts.copy_(torch.tensor(step, dtype=torch.int32))
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            with self.subTest(counts=step):
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(work, _eager_fill_dp_pad_rows(ids, counts, -1))
+                )
+
+    def test_fused_gate_masks_only_dp_pad_rows(self):
+        # The Triton router (fused shared expert) and the fast path it may take
+        # without one must both return the unmasked routes on real rows.
+        counts = torch.tensor([1, 0, 3, 2], device=self.DEVICE, dtype=torch.int64)
+        num_rows, num_experts = 3 * counts.numel(), 64
+        live = _dp_live_rows(num_rows, counts)
+        scores = torch.randn(num_rows, num_experts, device=self.DEVICE)
+        bias = 0.1 * torch.randn(num_experts, device=self.DEVICE)
+        for num_shared in (1, 0):
+            with self.subTest(num_fused_shared_experts=num_shared):
+                kwargs = dict(
+                    topk=8 + num_shared,
+                    num_fused_shared_experts=num_shared,
+                    routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
+                )
+                weights_all, ids_all = moe_fused_gate(scores, bias, **kwargs)
+                weights, ids = moe_fused_gate(
+                    scores, bias, dp_real_rows=counts, **kwargs
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(ids[live], ids_all[live]))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(weights[live], weights_all[live]))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(ids[~live] == -1))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(weights[~live] == 0))
+
+    def test_fused_moe_skips_dp_pad_rows(self):
+        # Under a DP-gathered forward, select_experts routes the padding rows to
+        # -1, in the Triton router (the biased sigmoid paths, grouped as
+        # GLM-5.3-Flash configures it, with a fused shared expert) or after it
+        # (softmax); the TP fused MoE then returns zeros there and real rows
+        # unchanged.
+        set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"))
+        num_experts, hidden, inter = 16, 256, 128
+        counts = torch.tensor([1, 0, 3, 2], device=self.DEVICE, dtype=torch.int64)
+        num_rows = 3 * counts.numel()
+        live = _dp_live_rows(num_rows, counts)
+        x = torch.randn(num_rows, hidden, device=self.DEVICE).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        logits = torch.randn(num_rows, num_experts, device=self.DEVICE)
+        # One more expert for the fused shared slot (id num_experts).
+        w1 = torch.randn(num_experts + 1, 2 * inter, hidden, device=self.DEVICE)
+        w2 = torch.randn(num_experts + 1, hidden, inter, device=self.DEVICE)
+        w1 = (w1 / hidden**0.5).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        w2 = (w2 / inter**0.5).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        bias = 0.1 * torch.randn(num_experts, device=self.DEVICE)
+        shared = SharedExpertsConfig(num_fused_shared_experts=1)
+        configs = {
+            "softmax": TopKConfig(top_k=4, renormalize=False),
+            "sigmoid_shared": TopKConfig(
+                top_k=4 + 1,
+                shared_experts=shared,
+                correction_bias=bias,
+                scoring_func="sigmoid",
+                routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
+                allow_routed_experts_capture=False,
+            ),
+            # More than 8 routed slots takes the grouped path's Triton router.
+            "grouped_sigmoid_shared": TopKConfig(
+                top_k=9 + 1,
+                use_grouped_topk=True,
+                num_expert_group=1,
+                topk_group=1,
+                shared_experts=shared,
+                correction_bias=bias,
+                scoring_func="sigmoid",
+                routed_scaling_factor=2.5,
+                allow_routed_experts_capture=False,
+            ),
+        }
+        for name, topk_config in configs.items():
+            with self.subTest(router=name):
+                routed_all = select_experts(
+                    hidden_states=x, router_logits=logits, topk_config=topk_config
+                )
+                prev = set_forward_context(
+                    ForwardContext(attn_backend=None, moe_dp_real_rows=lambda: counts)
+                )
+                try:
+                    routed = select_experts(
+                        hidden_states=x, router_logits=logits, topk_config=topk_config
+                    )
+                finally:
+                    set_forward_context(prev)
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(routed.topk_ids[live], routed_all.topk_ids[live])
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(routed.topk_ids[~live] == -1))
+                out_all = fused_moe(x, w1, w2, routed_all)
+                out = fused_moe(x, w1, w2, routed)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out[live], out_all[live]))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.all(out[~live] == 0))
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
